extracted.intended_audience: Owners of HUD-assisted properties, Public Housing Agencies (PHAs), contract administrators, property managers, and HUD program staff responsible for Section 8 project-based assistance and HUD-assisted housing inspections and compliance.
extracted.subtask_description: Regulatory standards and procedures for admission preferences, income reexaminations, family verification, approval of security personnel occupancy, physical condition (NSPIRE) standards, inspection procedures, timing, scoring, and self-inspections for HUD-assisted and Section 8 project-based housing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Admission preferences (residency, working families, disabilities, victims, single persons)
rubrics_metrics.description: Owners may adopt preferences for admission including residency preference areas, working families, families including a person with disabilities, victims of domestic violence (owner should consider), and preference for single persons who are elderly, displaced, homeless, or persons with disabilities over other single persons. The working family preference must not be based on amount of earned income. An applicant qualifies for the working family preference if the head/spouse/sole member is age 62 or older or is a person with disabilities. An owner may not adopt a preference for persons with a specific disability.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Includes the requirement that education/training program participants can be treated as residents of a residency preference area if program prepares them for the job market. These admission preference options are discretionary to owners but constrained by anti-discrimination limits (e.g., no preference for a specific disability, no income-amount-based working-family preference).

rubrics_metrics.name: Annual reexamination requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: The owner must conduct a reexamination and redetermination of family income and composition at least annually for Section 8 project-based assistance programs (except moderate rehabilitation and project-based voucher programs).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applies to reexamination of family income and composition; establishes a baseline cadence (annual) for owners to reassess eligibility and rent determinations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Interim reexamination: timing and reasonable time standard
rubrics_metrics.description: A family may request an interim reexamination for changes since the last exam. The owner must conduct any interim reexamination within a reasonable time after the family request or when the owner becomes aware of an increase in family adjusted income. 'Reasonable time' may vary with verification time but generally should not exceed 30 days from the date a family reports changes in income to an owner.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reasonable time depends on verification complexity; the 30-day guideline is generally expected for timely reporting of changes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Interim reexamination: declines for small decreases and threshold for increases
rubrics_metrics.description: Owner may decline to conduct an interim reexamination if estimated decreased adjusted income is less than ten percent of annual adjusted income (or lower HUD/owner-established threshold). Owner must conduct an interim reexamination when aware that adjusted income has changed by an amount estimated to increase annual adjusted income by ten percent or more (or other HUD-established amount), with specific exceptions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Exceptions: (i) do not consider earned income increases when estimating unless family previously received an interim reduction during certification period; (ii) owner may choose not to conduct an interim reexamination in the last three months of a certification period.

rubrics_metrics.name: Owner policies on reporting changes
rubrics_metrics.description: The owner must adopt policies, consistent with the interim reexamination rules, prescribing when and under what conditions the family must report a change in family income or composition.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Owners must publish/maintain clear written policies describing reporting obligations to families so timing and conditions for reporting are consistent with regulation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Effective date of rent changes and notice requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: If a family reports a change timely per owner policy, owner must provide 30 days advance notice of any rent increase, which becomes effective the first day of the month after the 30-day notice period. Rent decreases effective first day of the first month after the change date. If family failed to report timely, owners must implement rent increases retroactively to the first of the month following the change; rent decreases must be implemented no later than the first rent period following reexamination but may be applied retroactively at owner's discretion under written policy and subject to limits.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A retroactive rent decrease may not be applied prior to the later of: (A) the first of the month following the date of the change leading to the interim reexamination, or (B) the effective date of the family's most recent previous interim or annual reexamination (or initial exam if that was last).

rubrics_metrics.name: Streamlined income determination: election and eligibility
rubrics_metrics.description: An owner may elect to apply a streamlined income determination to families receiving fixed income as defined by the rule (periodic payments at reasonably predictable levels, e.g., Social Security, SSI, SSDI, pensions, annuities, other COLA-adjustable receipts).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Election is optional for owners; applies only to families whose income meets the 'fixed income' definition.

rubrics_metrics.name: Streamlined income determination: fixed income definition
rubrics_metrics.description: 'Fixed income' means periodic payments at reasonably predictable levels from sources including Social Security, SSI, SSDI; federal/state/local/private pensions; annuities, retirement benefits, insurance/disability/death benefits; or other income subject to adjustment by a verifiable COLA or current interest rate.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: List is illustrative; the key is periodicity, predictability, and verifiable adjustment mechanism (COLA/interest rate).

rubrics_metrics.name: Streamlined income determination: method and 90% threshold
rubrics_metrics.description: Owners using streamlined determination must adjust family income according to the percentage of unadjusted income that is fixed income. If 90% or more of unadjusted income is fixed income, owner must apply a COLA to fixed-income sources provided family certifies 90%+ fixed income and unchanged sources; non-fixed income need not be adjusted. If less than 90% fixed, owner must apply COLA to each fixed source and determine other income per regular rules.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Family certification is required for the >=90% treatment; different procedures apply depending on the fixed-income share.

rubrics_metrics.name: Streamlined income determination: COLA rate and verification
rubrics_metrics.description: Owners must use a COLA or current interest rate that applies to each specific fixed-income source from a public source or tenant-provided third-party documentation; if no public or tenant docs exist, owner must obtain third-party verification. For any income determined under streamlined method, owner must obtain third-party verification of all income amounts every 3 years.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Requires documented sources for COLA rates; triennial third-party verification is mandatory for incomes determined through streamlined process.

rubrics_metrics.name: De minimis errors in income calculation
rubrics_metrics.description: An owner will not be considered out of compliance solely due to de minimis errors where the owner determination differs from correct determination by no more than $30 per month ($360 annually) in adjusted income per family. Owner must correct errors once aware. Owner must credit/repay families if overcharged due to de minimis error; families are not required to repay if owner undercharged. HUD may revise the de minimis amount through rulemaking.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: De minimis tolerances relieve strict liability for trivial mathematical/clerical differences but do not absolve obligation to correct and make repayments where families overcharged.

rubrics_metrics.name: Family obligation to supply information
rubrics_metrics.description: Families must supply any information HUD or the owner determines necessary for Section 8 administration, including evidence of citizenship/eligible immigration status, any information requested for regular or interim reexaminations, and must ensure information is true and complete.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Information includes certifications, releases, or other documentation. Non-compliance or false information would violate family obligations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Family release and consent for verification
rubrics_metrics.description: As a condition of admission or continued occupancy, owner must require the family head and designated members to execute a HUD-approved release and consent authorizing depositories, private income sources, or Federal/State/local agencies to furnish information to the owner or HUD as necessary. Use/disclosure of such information shall be limited to purposes directly connected with Section 8 administration.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Includes reference to forms required under §5.230; limits on use protect privacy and confine disclosures to program administration.

rubrics_metrics.name: Owner responsibility for third-party verification
rubrics_metrics.description: Except as allowed under limited exceptions, the owner must obtain and document in the family file third-party verification of reported family annual income, the value of assets, expenses related to deductions from annual income, and other factors affecting adjusted income, or document why third-party verification was not available.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Third-party verification is the default expectation; documentation of attempts or reasons for lack of third-party verification must be kept in the file.

rubrics_metrics.name: Verification of assets exception and triennial verification
rubrics_metrics.description: For families with net family assets equal to or less than $50,000 (adjusted annually by HUD), an owner may accept a family's declaration for recertification purposes, except the owner must obtain third-party verification of all family assets every 3 years.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Owner may use declaration for lower-asset families but must still perform triennial third-party verification; the $50,000 threshold is CPI-adjusted annually.

rubrics_metrics.name: Approval criteria and application requirements for security personnel occupancy
rubrics_metrics.description: An owner may apply to the contract administrator to lease an available Section 8 unit to police or qualified security personnel (who would not otherwise be eligible) for the purpose of increasing project security. The owner's written application must include: description of criminal activity and effect on resident security; qualifications and period of residence of security personnel and proposed background checks; full disclosure of any family relationship to owner; explanation of how residency increases security; rent payable details and other compensation; terms of occupancy; and other information requested.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Definitions provided for 'security personnel' and 'police officer' and for 'security' purposes; application must demonstrate security benefit and disclose conflicts of interest.

rubrics_metrics.name: Contract administrator discretion and approval conditions for security occupancy
rubrics_metrics.description: The contract administrator has discretion to approve or disapprove the owner's application and may impose conditions. Notice of approval will specify the term and approval may be withdrawn if occupancy is not providing adequate security benefits or benefits are not a sufficient return for program costs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Approval is discretionary and conditioned on continued security benefit; contract administrator may reassess and withdraw approval.

rubrics_metrics.name: Housing assistance payment and rent treatment for security personnel occupancy
rubrics_metrics.description: During approved occupancy by security personnel, the monthly housing assistance payment equals the contract rent minus the amount of rent payable monthly by the security personnel as approved by the contract administrator. The owner bears the risk of collecting rent from security personnel and is not entitled to any vacancy payment during such occupancy. Contract administrator may consider whether security services are adequate return for housing assistance or if costs should be borne by owner from other project income.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Owner cannot increase HAP because of non-payment by security personnel; contract administrator may judge the cost/benefit of the arrangement when approving rent offsets.

rubrics_metrics.name: National standards for condition of HUD housing (NSPIRE): general functional requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: Items and components inside, outside, and within HUD housing units must be functionally adequate, operable, and free of health and safety hazards. For HCV, PBV, and Moderate Rehabilitation programs, standards apply to the subsidized unit itself and items/components within primary/secondary means of egress, common features related to residential use, and systems equipment that directly service the subsidized unit.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Sets the overall performance objective of safe, habitable dwellings; clarifies scope differences for tenant-based and project-based programs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Inside area standards
rubrics_metrics.description: Inside common areas and building systems must meet affirmative requirements: at least one battery-operated or hard-wired smoke detector on each level; carbon monoxide detection standards as set by Secretary (except certain exempt housing); outlets within 6 feet of a water source must be GFCI protected; guardrails for elevated walking surfaces with vertical drop >=30 inches; permanently mounted light fixtures in kitchens and each bathroom; no unvented gas/oil/kerosene space heaters.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples of inside areas include basements, corridors, community rooms, mechanical rooms, etc. Secretary may establish additional standards via Federal Register notice.

rubrics_metrics.name: Outside area standards
rubrics_metrics.description: Outside areas (site, exterior components, grounds) must have outlets within 6 feet of a water source GFCI protected, and must have guardrails where there is an elevated walking surface with a vertical drop of 30 inches or greater.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples include fencing, lighting, walkways, roofs, windows, detached garages, play areas, etc.

rubrics_metrics.name: Unit (dwelling unit) standards
rubrics_metrics.description: Units must include hot and cold running water in bathroom and kitchen (adequate safe drinking water), have a bathroom/sanitary facility with sink, bathtub/shower, and interior flushable toilet; include smoke detectors per specified locations (each level, inside bedrooms, within 21 feet of a bedroom door along path of travel, living area side if separated by door), hearing-impaired alarm requirements, living room and kitchen with sink, cooking appliance, refrigerator, food prep and storage, occupancy density (at least one bedroom or living/sleeping room for each two persons for HCV/PBV), CO detection standards, two working outlets or one outlet+permanent light in habitable rooms, GFCI for outlets within 6 feet of water, permanently installed heating for designated climate zones, no unvented space heaters burning gas/oil/kerosene, guardrails for elevated surfaces >=30 inches, and permanently mounted light fixtures in kitchen and each bathroom.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: NFPA 72 compliance satisfies smoke detector specs; Secretary may add standards via Federal Register notification; certain exemptions for housing covered only through §§5.701(a)(6) or (7).

rubrics_metrics.name: Health and safety hazards: required absence and lead paint compliance
rubrics_metrics.description: Inside, outside, and units must be free of health and safety hazards (including but not limited to carbon monoxide, electrical hazards, extreme temperature, flammable/fire hazards, garbage/debris, handrail hazards, infestation, lead-based paint, mold, structural soundness). HUD housing must comply with lead-based paint evaluation/control requirements and maintain proper documentation per 24 CFR part 35 and applicable statutes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Enumerates types of hazards considered in inspections; cross-references lead paint statutes and 24 CFR part 35 for specific responsibilities and documentation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Compliance with State and local codes
rubrics_metrics.description: NSPIRE standards do not supersede State and local housing codes. All HUD housing other than units assisted under HCV and PBV must comply with State or local housing codes to comply with this subpart. State/local code compliance is not part of the determination of whether a unit passes NSPIRE standards for HCV and PBV programs (except per §5.705(a)(3)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Program-specific regulations may require additional compliance; clarifies interplay between federal inspection standards and local code enforcement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of alternative inspections or additional PBV standards
rubrics_metrics.description: A PHA relying on an alternative inspection under 24 CFR 982.406 is not subject to the NSPIRE standards set by this section. PHAs may elect to establish additional PBV requirements for quality, architecture, or design which must be specified in the Agreement to enter into a HAP Contract or HAP Contract as provided in 24 CFR part 983.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Allows program-specific flexibility where equivalent/alternative inspection systems exist or where PHAs set higher PBV standards in contractual agreements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Inspection procedures and deficiency scoring
rubrics_metrics.description: Entities responsible for inspections must inspect and score HUD housing per Secretary standards published in the Federal Register. Inspecting entities shall identify each deficiency as 'Life Threatening', 'Severe', 'Moderate', or 'Low.' The inspection scope generally requires inside, outside and unit inspections per §5.703.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Scoring methodology and procedures are determined by Secretary notice (Federal Register). Deficiency categories drive timelines and remediation priorities.

rubrics_metrics.name: HCV and PBV inspection criteria variation approval
rubrics_metrics.description: HUD may approve inspection criteria variations that apply local housing codes or account for local climatic/geographic conditions if the variations either meet or exceed performance requirements or significantly expand affordable housing opportunities. HUD will not approve variations likely to adversely affect health/safety or severely restrict housing choice. Approved variations must be added to the Administrative Plan.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Variations require HUD approval and must be included in PHA Administrative Plan (24 CFR 982.54(d)(21)); approval conditions protect resident health/safety and housing choice.

rubrics_metrics.name: Entities responsible for conducting inspections
rubrics_metrics.description: The owner, lender, contract administrator, or HUD is generally responsible for performing inspections of HUD housing as provided in law, regulatory agreement, or contract. For properties with multiple HUD-insured loans, only the first mortgage lender is required to conduct the inspection and must provide the report to the second lender. Under HCV and PBV, PHAs are responsible unless another entity is assigned; PHA-owned units receiving section 8(o) assistance must be inspected by an independent entity as specified in parts 982 and 983. Under Moderate Rehabilitation, PHA is generally responsible unless managing units with a HAP contract where HUD inspects per 24 CFR 882.516(d).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specifies default inspection responsibilities and exceptions across program types; emphasizes independent inspection requirement for PHA-owned assisted units.

rubrics_metrics.name: Timing and frequency of inspections and extended inspection cycles
rubrics_metrics.description: A property must be inspected before approval for program participation and generally must be inspected annually. Inspections shall be conducted no earlier than 3 months before and no later than 3 months after the anniversary of the previous inspection (previously 6 months window for inspections due on or before July 1, 2024). HUD may approve extensions for good cause. HUD will score/rank properties and, based on scores, assign inspection cycles: Standard 1 (90+ points) => inspection once every 3 years; Standard 2 (80-89.99) => once every 2 years; Standard 3 (<80) => annual inspection. Additional specific cycles apply for small rural PHAs, small PHAs, HCV/PBV voucher inspections per other parts, and exemptions possible for certain Section 232 facilities.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Establishes inspection cadence tied to performance scoring; includes special rules for certain PHA sizes and program-specific frequencies.

rubrics_metrics.name: Inspection costs and reinspection fees
rubrics_metrics.description: The cost of an inspection is the responsibility of the entity responsible for inspection, except a reasonable fee may be required of the owner for a reinspection if owner-notified repairs are found uncorrected at reinspection. No inspection or reinspection fee may be passed to the household residing in the unit(s).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Places inspection cost burden on inspecting entity; allows limited owner reinspection fees as a deterrent for failure to correct cited deficiencies.

rubrics_metrics.name: Access to property for inspection and score consequence for denial
rubrics_metrics.description: All owners and PHAs must provide HUD or HUD's representative with full and free access to all HUD-assisted properties and units for inspections, monitoring, and quality assurance reviews, whether or not resident is home or has installed additional locks not keyed by owner/PHA. Failure to provide access results in a physical condition score of zero for the project(s) involved, which will be used in calculating the physical condition indicator score and overall assessment for that owner or PHA.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Emphasizes unconditional access requirement and severe scoring penalty for denial of access.

rubrics_metrics.name: Tenant involvement in inspections
rubrics_metrics.description: HUD will establish, by notice, a procedure for tenants to recommend particular units for HUD to inspect. HUD may inspect and issue a report on these units, but such tenant-recommended inspections will not be included in the official score unless the units were randomly selected independent of the tenant recommendation. Owners/PHAs must correct any deficiency HUD identifies within HUD-established timeframes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provides a tenant-facing avenue to trigger HUD inspection and oversight while preserving the integrity of official sampling/scoring procedures.

rubrics_metrics.name: Uniform annual self-inspection requirement and recordkeeping
rubrics_metrics.description: All PHAs and owners of HUD housing subject to an assistance contract, other than owners participating in HCV, PBV, and Moderate Rehabilitation programs, are required to annually self-inspect their properties (including all units) to ensure maintenance in accordance with §5.703 standards. Owners/PHAs must maintain self-inspection results for three years and provide results to HUD upon request. This self-inspection is independent of other HUD inspections discussed in §5.705.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Mandates internal monitoring and records retention to support HUD oversight; exclusions for HCV/PBV/Moderate Rehab owners reflect program-specific inspection regimes.
